recognize_zh: 箭頭所指為中性球分葉核上以細絲相連、約 1.5 µm 的圓形緻密染色質小突起，形似鼓槌（drumstick），即女性 X 染色體失活形成的 Barr body。
features: Mature segmented neutrophil with four nuclear lobes
Small, round, dense chromatin appendage attached to one lobe by a fine strand (drumstick, arrow)
Appendage has a well-defined solid head and uniform dark staining
Neutrophil cytoplasm with fine pink granules
Background red cells normocytic with central pallor; occasional platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a mature segmented neutrophil bearing a small, round, dense chromatin appendage attached to a nuclear lobe by a thin filament. The appendage has a solid, sharply defined head, consistent with a drumstick. The background red cells and platelets are unremarkable. Findings represent a Barr body (inactivated X chromosome) in a neutrophil, a normal finding in females that is not of pathologic significance.

ddx.dx: Sessile nodule or small accessory lobe
ddx.vs: Sessile nodules are attached without a thin stalk and small lobes are larger and irregular, whereas a drumstick has a solid round head on a fine filament.
Racquet forms have a hollow (ring-like) head and small tags lack a discrete round head, and neither represents an inactive X chromosome.
These are detached basophilic cytoplasmic inclusions without a connecting strand to the nucleus, seen with immunosuppressive drugs or HIV.
A platelet lies separate from the nucleus with granular pale-purple texture instead of dense nuclear-chromatin staining connected by a filament.
